ephemerisVsHorizons.reference: JPL Horizons API (airless apparent azimuth/elevation of the target centre, DE441)

ephemerisVsApolloTables.reference: NASA Apollo Lunar Surface Journal, Sun/Earth altitude-azimuth tables (Nautical Almanac lunar ephemeris, 1970s)
ephemerisVsApolloTables.note: The 1970s tables place the Earth at infinity (no lunar-radius parallax, up to 0.26 deg). Without parallax we match them; with parallax, as Horizons and this project do, the difference equals the parallax.
ephemerisVsApolloTables.excludedAzimuthEntry: Apollo 12 EVA1 end (out of sequence in the source table, 0.41 deg off)

horizonAlgorithm.method: Ray marching over LOLA DEMs in the plane Moon-centre/observer/sample (exact curvature)
analyticTests: smooth sphere gives the geometric dip -acos(R/(R+mast)) in every azimuth
a 500 m ridge 10 km away appears at the analytic angle (0.08 deg tolerance)
a higher mast sees lower; NaN samples are ignored
a 10 deg plane returns a 10 deg slope
